title: Pinwheel motif — basic
subtitle: A flat hexagonal motif with six angled blade sections worked in the round
excerpt: Six blade sections radiate from the centre ring and angle across the motif in the same direction, giving the pinwheel its rotating appearance. Each blade is a treble cluster worked into the previous round at an offset, pulling the fabric into the characteristic twist that holds flat after blocking.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 3 (1888), pinwheel motif construction (Internet Archive). Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), rotating-blade motif section.
heroPrompt: A basic pinwheel crochet motif in two shades of teal DK cotton on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight. Six angled blade sections visible radiating from the centre, 11 cm across.

crochet.gaugeText: Finished pinwheel motif measures 11 cm across in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Pinwheel motif — basic
chartDefinition.caption: Six blade sections angle clockwise from the centre ring. Each round adds one treble to each blade tip, extending the rotate pattern outward.

glossaryTerms.definition: One of the six angled arms of a pinwheel motif. Each blade is formed by working treble clusters into offset chain spaces on successive rounds, pulling the fabric into a clockwise twist.

content.text: The pinwheel motif works treble clusters into offset chain spaces on each round, twisting six

clockwise as the motif grows. The offset is small — each cluster enters the chain space from the adjacent blade rather than its own — but the cumulative effect across three rounds gives a clear propeller shape.
Use two colours to make the blades stand out: work rounds 1 and 2 in colour A and the border round in colour B. Block firmly — the offset construction wants to cup slightly before pinning flat.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 8 g DK-weight cotton across one or two colours. A 4 mm hook. Tapestry needle, scissors, blocking mat, pins.

content.text: Magic ring. Ch 3 (counts as first tr). 1 tr into ring. *Ch 1, 2 tr into ring.* Rep from * 4 more times. Ch 1, sl st to top of beg ch-3. Pull to close ring. (12 tr, 6 ch-1 spaces.)

Sl st into first ch-1 sp. Ch 3 (counts as first tr). Work 2 more tr into the NEXT ch-1 sp (offset one space clockwise). *Ch 1, skip back one ch-1 sp, 3 tr into the following ch-1 sp.* Rep from * 4 more times. Ch 1, sl st to top of beg ch-3. (18 tr, 6 ch-1 spaces.)
Join (or continue) border colour. *3 dc into the next ch-1 sp. Ch 2.* Rep from * around all 6 sp. Sl st to join. (18 dc, 6 ch-2 arches.)
Add two more rounds with the offset method for the lacy pinwheel, or work a fourth round of trebles per blade for the dense pinwheel.
